item.title: Six Flags X2 rollercoaster demolished after report exposed brain injuries and deaths
item.description: Six Flags has said its X2 rollercoaster, enjoyed by more than 16 million people, is to be demolished after a report into deaths, comas and injuries
item.author: Paige Ingram
item.media:keywords: America (section), Health (section), Six Flags Magic Mountain, X2 rollercoaster, brain injuries, ride safety concerns

media:content.media:description: Pictured: The X2 roller coaster is famous for it’s rotating seats and high speedsA 22-year-old man died from a traumatic brain injury he suffered from being violently shaken around on a popular Six Flags rollercoaster, according to a lawsuit filed by his family.Recent San Diego State graduate Christopher Hawley was in “excellent health” when he went to Six Flags Magic Mountain in Los Angeles with his younger brother and a cousin on June 23, 2022 — just to collapse soon after riding the X2 rollercoaster, according to a wrongful death suit seeking $10 million.https://nypost.com/2025/03/19/us-news/grad-died-from-traumatic-brain-injury-from-six-flags-ride-lawsuit/
